response_dtos.login: LoginSessionDto: UserProfile + role + menus + explicit token/deviceId only here
response_dtos.admin_user_info: UserInfoDto: UserProfile + role + menus; must not expose credentials
response_dtos.role_reads: RoleInfoDto/RoleMenusDto; do not return raw user credentials

frontend_session_chain.request_headers: src/common/http/index.js reads localStorage token/deviceId and adds both headers
frontend_session_chain.logout_flow: src/common/session/logout.js calls userLoginOut, then closes WS/serial/public sockets and clears token/deviceId/userInfo/userRole/userRouter
frontend_session_chain.auth_failure_handling: src/common/http/index.js maps 203/204/206 to login/session prompts; it must remain unchanged during Rust migration
frontend_session_chain.route_guard: src/config/router/guards.js clears session keys and routes anonymous users to /login

security_invariants: REST token/deviceId are header-only; no query fallback
WS query credentials remain a separate unchanged protocol
token is opaque and database stores SHA-256 digest
is_admin=0 is administrator; policy checks existence of an admin role
client userId is never an authentication source
password/token/deviceId never appear in non-login response DTOs
logout invalidates the token and preserves local cleanup even if network logout fails

rust_auth_context_design.sources: validated token/deviceId headers plus database role existence query
rust_auth_context_design.traffic: none; Java remains sole production implementation
rust_auth_context_design.rollback: route complete auth domain back to Java :18001 before any Rust writes

not_yet_implemented: Rust password hash migration and legacy compatibility
Rust gateway route or canary configuration
production user fixture or traffic cutover
